home.ios.install.title: Install Backpacker
home.ios.install.copy: On iPhone, the Home Screen version stores data separately from Safari. Saving access with email will bring your trips into the installed app.
home.ios.install.open.as.app: Turn on Open as Web App, then tap Add.
home.install.ios.hint: On iPhone: Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen
home.install.browser.hint: Open the browser menu and choose Add to Home Screen
home.support.product.body.origin: BACKPACKER grew out of real trip planning: when you want to bring events, places to visit, bookings, and ideas together in one place instead of jumping between different sources to find website links, notes, and spreadsheets.
home.support.product.body.planning: BACKPACKER helps you quickly sketch out a trip plan, arrange event and place cards by day, see the budget clearly, keep ideas from getting lost, and comfortably return to editing the trip from your phone.
home.support.product.body.ideas: You can collect ideas and wish-list items in advance, even before a trip exists. Tickets and bookings can be attached to cards. You can share the plan and budget with travel companions by link.
home.support.product.body.extension: You can add ideas manually or collect them straight from the browser with the Backpacker Chrome extension.
home.support.product.body.sync: Save access with your email, and your trips, ideas, and attachments will stay the same on your phone and laptop.
home.support.product.release: Organizer Mode now includes program information, freshness, and participant materials.
home.support.howto.devices.title: Using Backpacker on multiple devices
home.support.howto.devices.body1: Save access with your email in your profile, and your personal trips will start syncing between devices. Your laptop, mobile browser, and installed app will show the same trip list.
home.support.howto.devices.body2: The first sign-in on a new device merges trips instead of replacing them: anything previously created on that device is combined with what is already in the cloud. Nothing is lost.
home.support.howto.devices.body3: If the same trip was edited differently on two devices—for example, while the phone was offline—Backpacker keeps both versions. A trip marked “copy from this device” will appear next to it, along with an explanation on Home.
home.support.howto.devices.body4: The app deliberately does not choose a winner, because that would require deleting someone's changes. Compare the versions, move what you need into one trip, and delete the extra one. Close the notice with the × button.
home.support.howto.devices.body5: Without a saved email, the app works as before: trips stay only in this browser and are not sent anywhere.
home.support.howto.devices.body6: The Trainer and trips under “Shared with me” are not synced: they are a demo and other people's trips.
home.support.howto.overview.title: Where everything is
home.support.howto.overview.body: Home contains the Trainer, the option to create a new trip, the “Ideas” section, and your trip feed. Inside a trip, you can arrange cards by day, move them to the idea parking area, change statuses, and view the budget.
home.support.howto.ideas.title: Ideas before a trip
home.support.howto.ideas.intro: The “Ideas” section on Home is a place for places, links, and wish-list items when no trip exists yet. It is useful for saving anything you find long before you have dates.
home.support.howto.ideas.item1: Ideas can be organized into collections or left without a collection.
home.support.howto.ideas.item2: An idea can have a type, link, location, price, and image.
home.support.howto.ideas.item3: You can turn an idea into a trip card: open it and tap “Add to trip”, then choose a trip and a day or “Unscheduled”. The card is created only after the usual save.
home.support.howto.ideas.item4: The original idea stays in place, so you can use it again.
home.support.howto.ideas.item5: Ideas you no longer need are archived, not permanently deleted.
home.support.howto.ideas.outro: Ideas live in the cloud and are tied to your saved email access, so they are visible on all your devices.
home.support.howto.extension.title: How to collect ideas from your browser
home.support.howto.extension.body: Backpacker has a Chrome extension for desktop. It lets you save useful finds while researching a trip instead of copying links and details by hand.
home.support.howto.extension.step1: Install Backpacker Travel Capture from the Chrome Web Store.
home.support.howto.extension.step2: Connect the extension to your Backpacker.
home.support.howto.extension.step3: On a page you want to keep, open the extension, review the captured card and send it to Backpacker.
home.support.howto.extension.step4: The find appears in Ideas, where you can later add it to any trip.
home.support.howto.extension.note: The extension saves only what you explicitly choose to save. A source link, title, image and detected price can be carried into the card when available, and remain editable.
home.support.howto.ai.title: Building a trip with AI
home.support.howto.ai.item1: On Home, tap “Create new trip” and choose “Build with AI”.
home.support.howto.ai.item2: Describe the trip in your own words: include the destination, dates or duration, participants, interests, pace, and important constraints. You can type the text or dictate it.
home.support.howto.ai.item3: AI will arrange ideas by day and prepare a preliminary draft. Check the title, dates, and cards before creating the trip.
home.support.howto.ai.item4: The trip appears only after you confirm it. It then becomes a normal editable trip: you can change cards, move them between days, add them, and delete them.
home.support.howto.ai.warning: AI can make mistakes or suggest inaccurate options, so double-check dates, prices, opening hours, and logistics.
home.support.howto.trainer.title: What the Trainer is for
home.support.howto.trainer.body: The Trainer is a ready-made demo trip. You can try days, cards, the budget, statuses, and export without risking your real trip.
home.support.howto.cards.title: Using cards
home.support.howto.cards.body: Open a card and set its type, price, status, date, time, and link. On mobile, you can move cards with a long press and swipe through the day tracks.
home.support.howto.attachments.title: Attachments: tickets and bookings
home.support.howto.attachments.intro: You can attach a file to a card—a ticket, voucher, or booking confirmation. Open the card and tap “Add attachment”.
home.support.howto.attachments.item1: PDF, JPG, PNG, and WebP files up to 10 MB are supported.
home.support.howto.attachments.item2: Attachments are stored in the cloud and available from any of your devices, so saved email access is required.
home.support.howto.attachments.item3: Files are visible only to you. Attachments are not included in a trip opened by link, so guests cannot see them.
home.support.howto.attachments.item4: You can remove an attachment from a card at any time.
home.support.howto.sharing.title: Traveling with friends
home.support.howto.sharing.item1: Open a trip, tap “Share”, then “Invite by link”, and copy the link.
home.support.howto.sharing.item2: A guest will see the trip in read-only mode, can save it under “Shared with me”, and open it later from Home.
home.support.howto.sharing.item3: If the budget is enabled, a guest can offer to cover part of an expense or add a new idea.
home.support.howto.sharing.item4: The trip changes only after the author decides: the author accepts or rejects suggestions in the “Suggestions” section inside the trip.
home.support.howto.sharing.item5: Personal trips without an open link are visible to no one else: they sync only between your devices.
home.support.howto.sharing.item6: Save access with your email so link management remains available after reinstalling the app and from another device. Without email, links are tied to the current browser session and cannot be recovered after reinstalling.
home.support.howto.iphone.title: Installing on iPhone
home.support.howto.iphone.body1: Open Backpacker in Safari, tap the system Share button, choose “Add to Home Screen”, turn on “Open as Web App”, and tap “Add”.
home.support.howto.iphone.body2: The app launched from the Home Screen stores data separately from Safari. If you already created trips in Safari, save access with your email in both places, and the trips will appear in the installed app automatically.
